text:
nina: FYI ran into a weird repro during onboarding: the quickstart JSON snippet in the README keeps failing for Windows users because CRLF line endings are being injected when they copy from GitHub web and paste into PowerShell. The request body ends up with literal \r characters and the API returns 400 / malformed JSON.

nina: Example shown in README (single-line pretty JSON):
```json
{"input": "hello", "options": {"max_tokens": 64}}
```

nina: When pasted into pwsh via VSCode terminal (CRLF), some shells send the payload with an extra \r which our server-side parser treats as invalid JSON in strict mode. New users hit a 400 and think the SDK is broken.

omar: Oof. I saw a similar issue last year where Docker on Windows normalized line endings in the build context and a curl payload was corrupted. Two quick mitigations: (1) recommend using ConvertTo-Json or a header-based Content-Type; (2) add a tiny troubleshooting note in the README about CRLF/paste behavior and using the sample script instead of inline copy/paste.

judy: Came across another UX wrinkle: the Console onboarding email includes a one-line cURL for quick validation. People copy it into Git Bash which is fine, but Codespaces users sometimes paste into the integrated terminal which interprets pasted newlines differently and botches the payload. Maybe we should avoid multi-line JSON inline in the email and instead link to the sample file.

nina: Proposed changes: (A) update README to provide a single-line escaped JSON curl example and a PowerShell-native snippet (ConvertTo-Json or Invoke-RestMethod), (B) add a short Troubleshooting item: "If you see 400 after pasting, try running the sample script instead of pasting inline JSON", and (C) tweak onboarding email to link to sample files rather than include full JSON blobs.

omar: For CI: our docs-snippet validator runs shellcheck + basic lint on ubuntu-latest only. We should add a windows-latest step that clones the samples, does a paste-sim test (cat sample.json | Invoke-RestMethod ...) and runs the quickstart scripts on pwsh to catch CRLF/paste regressions earlier. Also add a small job that builds the Docker sample on windows to catch any LF/CRLF transforms.

ci-bot: Draft workflow change proposed: docs/snippet-smoke -> matrix.os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest], with an additional job docs/snippet-docker-windows that builds samples/docker on windows-latest. Queueing proposal for maintainers.

judy: Also, doc rendering quirk: when GitHub shows the JSON block with soft-wrap it sometimes inserts zero-width spaces in copy-and-paste (specific to our docs theme). Suggest we run a small sanitizer on snippet text during docs build to strip invisible chars and unify line endings.

nina: Good call. Add a docs CI step to normalize snippets (strip non-printable chars, convert CRLF to LF in the canonical snippet artifacts) before running the smoke tests. That will help catch platform-conditional failures rather than shipping broken content.

omar: I'll open a PR for the CI changes and a small docs patch that replaces the inline multi-line JSON in onboarding email with a link to the sample file and a short PowerShell snippet.

docs-bot: Created DOCS-782: "Quickstart snippets: handle CRLF/paste issues, add Windows smoke tests, and sanitize snippet text in CI". Linked draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/812 (draft).

judy: One more small thing: add an explicit one-liner in the README "If you are on Windows and paste commands, prefer curl.exe or use PowerShell examples" so search hits from support link directly to that line.

nina: Thanks all. These are small docs/CI investments but will reduce noisy support tickets and confused first-day developers. :raised_hands:
